title: Enterprise reporting request decision-tree and onboarding checklist
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a decision-tree and onboarding checklist for enterprise console/reporting requests (usage analytics, cost breakdowns, large-scale exports, scheduled dashboards). The goal is to reduce triage time, set clear acceptance criteria, and standardize SLAs and escalation paths so engineering and support can consistently scope and deliver enterprise requests without repeated clarifying cycles.

Scope:
- New non-bug customer requests for reporting/exports/dashboards delivered via Console or SFTP/exports API
- Does NOT cover ad-hoc analytics performed by internal data teams or low-volume self-serve requests

Deliverables:
1) Decision-tree flow (yes/no path) for classifying requests into: self-serve, standard export, enterprise onboarding, or custom-engagement.
2) Onboarding checklist with required data-contract fields, minimal schema samples, and delivery templates.
3) Priority scoring heuristic (weights + buckets) that maps request signals to SLA lanes and expected engineering effort.
4) Escalation playbook (who to notify, stakeholder signoffs, security/data ownership gating).
5) Example intake form fields for Console to automate first-pass routing.

Decision-tree highlights:
- Step A: Is request achievable with existing Console exports or API? If yes -> self-serve path (lowest SLA).
- Step B: Does request include PII or regulated data? If yes -> require security gating and an on-prem/private deployment path evaluation.
- Step C: Is expected data volume > 1TB/month or >100K rows/export? If yes -> route to Enterprise exports lane with dedicated quota and signed DPA.
- Step D: Is real-time/near-real-time required (<=1m latency)? If yes -> mark as high-ops complexity; consider streaming or webhook alternatives.

Priority scoring heuristic (example):
- Customer revenue signal (paying ARR/contract size): weight 35
- Data volume/throughput: weight 20
- Security/regulatory requirement: weight 20
- Time sensitivity / legal/regulatory deadline: weight 15
- Implementation complexity (estimated points): weight 10
Final score 0-100 mapped to lanes: 0-29 P3 (self-serve), 30-59 P2 (standard export), 60-79 P1 (enterprise onboarding), 80-100 P0 (fast-track / executive escalation).

Onboarding checklist (required fields from requester):
- Business owner and primary contact (name, email, phone)
- Workspace ID and affected workspaces/accounts
- Data contract: list of fields, types, retention policy
- Example export payload (CSV/JSON sample, max 100 rows)
- Expected cadence (ad-hoc / hourly / daily / streaming)
- Estimated monthly volume (GB and rows)
- Destination (S3 bucket / GCS / SFTP / BigQuery) and access method + service account details
- Access/security constraints (PII, regional residency, encryption/KMS needs)
- Acceptance criteria (what success looks like for the customer)

Acceptance criteria for enterprise lane:
- Data contract validated and signed by customer data owner
- Security checklist cleared (if PII/regulatory) or security review scheduled
- Export tested with <5% data mismatch on initial sample and <1% on final delivery validation
- Delivery path documented and agreed (SLA for latency, retries/backoff, and retention)
- Rollout plan and rollback procedure attached

Trade-offs and notes:
- Strict gating reduces rework but may increase initial friction for customers; mitigations include templated forms and guided UX in Console.
- Tighter SLAs for enterprise lane increases operational costs; recommend reserving fast-track lane for contracts with revenue thresholds.
- We intentionally avoid building custom pipelines for every request; the decision-tree favors re-using export infrastructure wherever possible.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Feb 03: Draft decision-tree + intake form fields (this doc) -> PM review (Ava).
- Feb 07: Workshop with Eng, Security, Solutions (Rohan lead) to align on gating rules and feasibility.
- Feb 12: Prototype Console intake form + backend routing rule (ENG spike).
- Feb 20: Pilot with two enterprise customers (Solutions-led onboarding).
- Mar 01: Rollout documented playbook and update support runbook.

Metrics to measure success (first 90 days after rollout):
- Median triage time for enterprise reporting requests reduced from baseline by 40%
- Percentage of requests with complete onboarding checklist at first submission >= 70%
- Mean time-to-delivery for enterprise lane within promised SLA >= 90%
